content.text: how do i remove a home brew casks that does not exist

Use `brew uninstall --cask --force <cask-name>` first:

```bash
brew uninstall --cask --force bad-cask-name
```

If Homebrew says the cask doesn’t exist but it’s still listed/installed, clean stale references:

```bash
brew cleanup
brew doctor
```

If it is in your dotfiles `Brewfile`, remove or comment the cask line:

```bash
grep -n "bad-cask-name" packages/Brewfile
```

Then edit `packages/Brewfile`, remove:

```ruby
cask "bad-cask-name"
```

Then run:

```bash
brew bundle cleanup --file=packages/Brewfile
```

If the app still exists in `/Applications`, delete it manually:

```bash
rm -rf "/Applications/App Name.app"
```

To find what Homebrew thinks is installed:

```bash
brew list --cask
brew info --cask <cask-name>
```

If it’s a broken old cask token, this often fixes it:

```bash
brew untap homebrew/cask
brew tap homebrew/cask
brew update
brew cleanup
```
